subject.title: cli-backend agent runs against anthropic (claude-cli runtime) return 401 authentication_failed while identical claude invocation works in shell

question: Should OpenClaw change Claude CLI auth/env/refresh behavior for managed gateway runs, or first require a live macOS LaunchAgent plus loopback-MCP repro to isolate the 401 trigger?
rationale: The likely fixes cross auth-provider isolation and operator recovery policy, and current evidence proves the managed code path but not the live service-context failure mechanism.

options.title: Require live service-context repro
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask a maintainer with Claude CLI OAuth on macOS to compare managed cron/channel, same-service shell replay, live MCP, and empty MCP before code changes.

options.title: Treat as expired-token recovery overlap
options.body: Let the open re-auth hint PRs land for the narrower expired-token copy problem while keeping this issue open until the root managed-run failure is reproduced or ruled out.

options.title: Authorize an auth policy change now
options.body: Sponsor a maintainer-owned change to Claude CLI refresh/env handling with explicit upgrade/security proof for both default and failure modes.

recommendation.title: Require live service-context repro
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask a maintainer with Claude CLI OAuth on macOS to compare managed cron/channel, same-service shell replay, live MCP, and empty MCP before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to repeated ownership across Claude CLI stdio sessions, auth/env helper boundaries, and release-era runtime behavior.
